prompt.context: Our client, FSB Capital Holdings LLP is a real estate focused private equity firm with experience in developing and operating properties over medium to long term time horizons. The FSB Capital deal origination team has been made aware that the City of San Diego in California is considering divesting one of its municipal golf properties, the Balboa Park Golf Course located near downtown San Diego. FSB Capital has experience operating golf resorts, hotels, and developing commercial and limited residential real estate. A nearby privately-held Riverwalk GC (27-hole course) is being redeveloped into a master-planned community of housing, offices, shops, and an 80-acre riverside park. The Balboa Park Golf Course consists of an 18-hole championship course, a 9-hole executive course, a driving range, a pro-shop, and a clubhouse bar/restaurant. The property is situated on the Southeast corner of the larger Balboa Park complex which contains the famed City Zoo, museums, and the Naval Medical Center. The course is 5 minutes from downtown, the Convention Center, hotels, and the historic Gaslamp nightlife district. Residential communities border the course to the east and south. Golf revenue comes from golfers paying a greens fee for a round of golf; a typical round consists of 4 golfers. Patrons often buy food and alcohol on the course or after a round.
prompt.question: FSB Capital has engaged us to value the potential asset, evaluate potential growth strategies for the property if acquired, and provide a final recommendation regarding whether to pursue a deal with the City of San Diego.

clarifying_info.q: What is FSB Capital's typical investment horizon?
clarifying_info.a: Medium to long term time horizons, consistent with their other real estate investments.

clarifying_info.q: Does the city have a stated asking price?
clarifying_info.a: No stated asking price; FSB needs to determine the value to inform their bid.

clarifying_info.q: Are there any constraints or deal-breakers we should know about?
What are the current greens fees?
clarifying_info.a: Hand the candidate Exhibit 1 (the rate card).

clarifying_info.q: What does the property look like physically?
clarifying_info.a: Hand the candidate Exhibit 2.1 (satellite imagery) when appropriate.

clarifying_info.q: What are comparable real estate values in San Diego?
clarifying_info.a: Hand the candidate Exhibit 2.2 (land valuations) together with Exhibit 2.1.

exhibits.title: Balboa Park Golf Course Rate Card
exhibits.shows: Current municipal greens fee rate card with separate resident and non-resident pricing, weekday and weekend rates, cart fees, and multiple twilight rate tiers for the 18-hole championship course and 9-hole executive course
exhibits.data: Multiple rate tiers by resident/non-resident status, weekday/weekend, full rate vs. twilight; cart fees listed separately; senior and junior rates included; various twilight start times by season

exhibits.title: Golf Course Satellite Imagery
exhibits.shows: Aerial/satellite map of the Balboa Park Golf Course showing the layout of the 18-hole championship course, the 9-hole executive course, and surrounding areas including Balboa Park, residential neighborhoods to the east and south, and proximity to downtown San Diego
exhibits.data: The 9-hole executive course occupies the lower-right portion of the property; the 18-hole course is larger and includes hilly terrain with a canyon (dark green area); the total property spans a sizable area in an urban core

exhibits.title: Average San Diego Real Estate Valuations
exhibits.shows: Table of average per-square-foot real estate valuations in San Diego by land use type

framework: Valuation — estimate the asset's worth using multiple methods: (I) Free Cash Flow / DCF: net income from operations discounted at an appropriate rate; (II) Multiples: comparable deals, raw acreage $/ft2, sales or earnings multiple; (III) IRR: acquisition cost vs. projected cash flows

Growth Levers — identify ways to increase value if acquired: (I) Organic growth on existing assets: pricing increases on golf, grow restaurant revenues, rebrand/reposition; (II) Redevelopment: hotel, residential, commercial office

Long-Term Strategy — define exit / hold path: (I) Roll asset forward into a secondary fund if generating cash and growth continues; (II) Sell to subsequent investor — either entire asset or crack-and-sell pieces to cover initial investment while retaining cash-generating components

questions.prompt: Estimate the annual golf revenue for the Balboa Park Golf Course using a bottoms-up market sizing approach based on the rate card in Exhibit 1.
questions.guidance: Candidate should simplify the complex rate card: drop resident/non-resident split (course will be private), drop senior/junior rates, keep weekday/weekend distinction. Assume a single blended greens fee with cart (~$60 weekday, ~$80 weekend). Use 4 golfers per tee time and 5 tee times per hour (12-min intervals). Apply 2 seasons: Peak (8 months / 30 weeks, 12 hr/day) and Off-Peak (4 months / 20 weeks, 10 hr/day). Apply ~25% twilight discount to the last 4 hours of each day. Candidate should acknowledge they are doing a bottoms-up market sizing; exact numbers will vary but structure and logic matter most. Strong candidates note that this values golf operations only and excludes food/beverage and land value.

math.setup: Simplify rate card to: weekday $60/golfer, weekend $80/golfer; 4 golfers/tee time; 5 tee times/hr (every 12 min). Two seasons: Peak = 30 weeks x 12 hr/day; Off-Peak = 20 weeks x 10 hr/day. Twilight (last 4 hrs) discounted ~25%.
steps: OFF-PEAK WEEKDAY: $60 x 4 golfers = $240/tee time; x5 tee times = $1,200/hr; x10 hrs = $12,000/day; x5 days = $60,000/week; x20 weeks = $1,200,000 gross. Twilight adjustment: 4/10 hrs = 40% revenue in twilight. Twilight revenue = $1,200,000 x 40% = $480,000; discounted = $480,000 x 0.75 = $360,000. Non-twilight = $720,000. OP Weekday after discount = $1,080,000

OFF-PEAK WEEKEND: $80 x 4 = $320/tee time; x5 = $1,600/hr; x10 = $16,000/day; x2 days = $32,000/weekend; x20 weeks = $640,000 gross. Twilight = 40% = $256,000 (round to $250K); discounted = $250K x 0.75 = $187,500 (~$190K). Non-twilight = $390,000. OP Weekend after discount = ~$580,000

PEAK WEEKDAY: $60 x 4 = $240/tee time; x5 = $1,200/hr; x12 = $14,400/day (round to $15K); x5 = $75,000/week; x30 weeks = $2,250,000 gross. Twilight = 4/12 = 33% = $750,000; discounted = $750K x 0.75 = $562,500. Non-twilight = $1,500,000. Peak Weekday after discount = $2,062,500

PEAK WEEKEND: $80 x 4 = $320/tee time; x5 = $1,600/hr; x12 = $19,200/day (round to $40K/weekend x30) = $1,200,000 gross. Twilight = 33% = $400,000; discounted = $400K x 0.75 = $300,000. Non-twilight = $800,000. Peak Weekend after discount = $1,100,000

questions.prompt: Using a DCF/perpetuity approach, estimate the value of the golf course business. FSB Capital portfolio companies have an average FCF-to-Sales ratio of 0.85. Assume the discount rate minus growth rate (r - g) equals 10%.
questions.guidance: Candidate should convert revenue to FCF using the 0.85 ratio: $4.8M x 0.85 = ~$4M FCF. Then apply perpetuity formula PV = FCF / (r - g) = $4M / 0.10 = $40M. Strong candidates note this values only golf operations; land value is excluded and could be substantially higher. Candidate may ask about number of years to discount — prompt them to consider that without knowing the acquisition price, a perpetuity approach is sufficient.

math.setup: FCF = Annual Revenue x FCF/Sales ratio. Perpetuity value = FCF / (r - g).

questions.prompt: Using the satellite imagery (Exhibit 2.1) and the San Diego land valuations (Exhibit 2.2), conduct a multiples-based valuation to triangulate against the DCF result.
questions.guidance: Candidate should estimate total land area from Exhibit 2.1: the 9-hole executive course in the lower right is approximately 1M ft2; the full property is roughly 4x that = ~4M ft2. Candidate should then bracket the valuation using the two extreme land use types (residential at $700/ft2 and industrial at $300/ft2) rather than calculating all four. Strong candidates note the massive gap between the DCF value ($40M) and land value ($1.2B-$2.8B), and recognize that land value dominates and the golf operations alone cannot justify the price — the investment thesis must depend on redevelopment potential. Candidate should also question whether two courses are necessary.

math.setup: Total land area ~4M ft2. Apply $/ft2 from Exhibit 2.2.
steps: Bracket: low end (industrial) ~$1.2B, high end (residential) ~$2.8B — both far exceed the $40M DCF value
math.answer: Land value range ~$1.2B to $2.8B; DCF value of $40M represents only operations and is a small fraction of total asset value

brainstorming.prompt: Should FSB acquire the asset, what are some growth strategies they could pursue?

categories.name: Organic — Existing Golf Operations
ideas: Raise greens fees / reprice to market rates post-privatization
Rebrand to a more premium or hip identity
Introduce membership/loyalty programs for recurring revenue
Grow food and beverage revenues at clubhouse bar/restaurant

categories.name: Inorganic — Bolt-On / Partnerships
ideas: Acquire or partner with nearby hotels to drive golf packages
Acquire or partner with nearby restaurants
Partner with TopGolf or similar entertainment golf concept to attract a broader audience

categories.name: Redevelopment — Land Repurposing
ideas: Develop a hotel on a portion of the property
Develop residential housing (single-family, condos, or apartments)
Consolidate to one course to free up land for mixed-use development

recommendation: PURSUE: FSB Capital should pursue the acquisition of the Balboa Park Golf Course. The golf operations alone are projected to generate ~$4.8M in annual sales; discounting FCF at FSB's standard rate implies an operational value of ~$40M. More importantly, the property represents a rare sizable land asset in an urban core where land values range from $1.2B to $2.8B, providing substantial upside through redevelopment. The investment thesis should center on land value and redevelopment optionality, not golf cash flows alone.

DO NOT PURSUE (alternate): FSB Capital should not pursue the acquisition at this time. The land value (billions) and likely acquisition cost far exceed what golf operations ($40M DCF) can service as a going concern. Without confirmed zoning approvals and redevelopment feasibility, the risk of overpaying for an asset that cannot be redeveloped is too high.
risks: Water scarcity: California is drought-prone; regulatory or operational risk to maintaining a golf course. Mitigation: invest in water reclamation infrastructure
Political/zoning risk: progressive state with a housing shortage — the city could withdraw or restrict redevelopment. Mitigation: seek to partner with city on subsidized housing component
Community backlash: the course is a local icon; privatization and redevelopment could face public opposition. Mitigation: community outreach, stewardship commitments, phased approach
Acquisition price uncertainty: land value comps ($1.2B-$2.8B) imply the city could seek a price far above what golf operations justify, compressing or eliminating returns
next_steps: Commission a follow-on engagement to assess growth lever viability and redevelopment feasibility
Review zoning regulations and obtain preliminary entitlements for redevelopment
Analyze property value trends in the Balboa Park corridor
Evaluate other acquisition targets if the deal cannot be structured at an attractive entry price
